criteria.criterion: A test shows that when the merged commit is absent from the local object store but present on the remote, the merged-content check fetches it and returns the fingerprint instead of failing with 'not a tree object'. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: The test pr::tests::a_merged_commit_missing_locally_is_fetched_before_it_is_fingerprinted passed. It clones an origin, then commits on the origin only, and asserts the clone's rev_parse(merged) is None. It then asserts that GitContent::fingerprint_of returns the origin's fingerprint, and that the clone's for-each-ref output and HEAD did not change.

criteria.criterion: A test shows that `land_pr` with an existing open PR link, a host that reports the PR merged, and a landed commit not reachable from the local head confirms the landing and does not return 'not landed on this branch'. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: The test gh::tests::a_merged_pull_request_confirms_the_landing_though_the_landed_commit_is_off_this_branch passed. Its setup: a stored open link, landed_commit failing with 'not landed on this branch', and a host that reports merged1. It asserts that confirm_existing_merge returns Landed, stores the link, pushes nothing and requests no merge. Athena::land_pr sends the landed_commit error to this function (gh.rs:576-610). The test calls the helper, not Athena::land_pr end to end; see the finding.

criteria.criterion: A test shows that with no stored link and no landed commit on the branch, `land_pr` still errors with 'not landed on this branch'. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: The test gh::tests::an_open_pull_request_or_no_link_keeps_the_not_landed_error passed. With no link, confirm_existing_merge returns None and the host is never asked. landed_commit fails with 'not landed on this branch', and the dispatch then returns that error (`None => Err(not_landed)`). An open, unmerged link also returns None.

criteria.criterion: `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, and `cargo fmt --check` all pass.
criteria.evidence: All three ran in one && chain and all succeeded. Clippy printed no warnings, and every test binary reported ok with 0 failed.

criteria.criterion: docs/design/native-pr-landing.md states that merge commits are the landing shape for pull requests, and that squash merges break ancestry.
criteria.evidence: New section §5.2a says: 'Merge commits are the landing shape for pull requests' and '**Squash merges break ancestry.**', with the reason and the #39 example.

criteria.criterion: docs/decisions.md has a new entry after D86 that records merge commits as the PR landing shape. It cites the #39 squash conflict and the simulated two-merge-commit history passing `athena check --history` with 0 violations.
criteria.evidence: D87 is appended after D86. Its Provenance cites the PR #39 squash ancestry break, the conflict in the next PR, and the simulated two merge-commit history passing `athena check --history` with 0 violations. It labels this as evidence the user reported that was not re-run here.

criteria.criterion: The fetch uses the existing Git wrapper and does not move any local branch or ref other than fetching the object.
criteria.evidence: Git::ensure_commit in athena-git uses self.run to call `fetch --quiet --no-tags --no-write-fetch-head --refmap= <remote> <oid>`, and only when rev_parse says the commit is missing. With an empty refmap and no refspec destination, no ref is updated. Tests in athena-git and pr.rs assert that for-each-ref and HEAD are unchanged.

findings.summary: No test calls Athena::land_pr itself, so the new dispatch to confirm_existing_merge is covered only by reading the code.
findings.evidence: The tests call confirm_existing_merge and landed_commit separately. If the `Err(not_landed) => match confirm_existing_merge(...)` arm were reverted to plain `?`, every test would still pass. The arm is short and reads correctly.

findings.summary: crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs was listed as a deliverable but is unchanged.
findings.evidence: The diff stat has no display.rs. The existing display of PrReport already covers the new path, so no change is needed.

summary: The change does all three things you asked for. (1) `athena land --pr` now fetches the merged commit itself before checking it: `GitContent::fingerprint_of` calls a new `Git::ensure_commit`, which fetches only that commit and moves no branch or ref. A test with a real clone and remote shows the fetch and checks that no ref moved. (2) When the job's landed commit is not on the current branch but its PR link exists, `Athena::land_pr` now asks the host first, through the new `confirm_existing_merge`. A merged PR is confirmed as landed (or as merged but unverified). With no link, or an open PR, you still get 'not landed on this branch'. Tests cover the merged, other-content and no-link/open cases. (3) docs/design/native-pr-landing.md §5.2a, a note in athena-v0.md §7.3 and a new decision D87 record merge commits as the PR landing shape. D87 cites the #39 squash conflict and the 0-violation simulated history, and marks both as your reported evidence, not re-run. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core` (72 passed), plus `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test --workspace`, all clean. One small gap: no test runs `Athena::land_pr` end to end, so the new hand-off to the host check is checked only by reading the code, which is short and correct. Verdict: pass.
